title: Re: Blackcat – Yet Another Personal Agent...
text: I tried organising my personal life with openclaw and claudeclaw but didn't like it very much. I been coding for over 30 years so I figured I should build one myself. It would have taken me months but with claude code I was able to do it in a few weekends. It essentially keeps a local copy of messages from whatsup, telegram, Gmail ( mail and calenders) , creates a vector index so that its searchable. I can create schedules to periodically scan and make daily briefings, reminders etc. I made a plugin interface so it was easy to integrated home assistant, unifi network, remote ssh, allsky so far. The github readme has some demo gifs.
author: vpuna

title: Re: Gauze Corrects LLM Responses...
text: If you have worked with open-weight/local LLMs, you've known both the highs and the lows. Lows there are many: malformed response tags, empty responses, stuck loops, overthinking, inference engine errors and much more. You don't notice those when using commercial models, because the vendors iron out those quirks in their gateways, but you're left standing when using free models. Gauze is a transparent openAI compatible gateway which monitors and corrects bad LLM responses.
author: ggeorgovassilis

title: Show HN: Peer-to-peer instant messaging with proof-of-work spam protection
text:
Bitmessage.org still doesn't support Python 3 and over the years I've tried several times to create something similar but each time have run up against unclear/incomplete/missing documentation in Python/Rust/flask/tokio/asyncio/etc. Finally decided to give ChatGPT a real try and with tutoring based on minimal examples managed to have something usable in about a day. Most "difficult" part was having two instances of flask/quart running simultaneously while also having other stuff happen periodically in background.

Novel thing in p2pIM compared to Bitmessage is that messages' PoW decays and that larger messages require better PoW than smaller ones. Thus small messages that are discarded quickly require significantly less PoW than large messages that persist for a long time. p2pIM doesn't support encryption but that should be straightforward to build on top.

Message_v0 class in https://github.com/iljah/p2pIM/blob/main/messages.py defines low level details such as PoW, how many bytes to use for nonce, checksum, etc. Currently they're all only about 10 bytes or hex characters for easier debugging and testing. PoW is calculated as sha256 of timestamp+nonce+checksum, where checksum is sha256 of payload. Adding channel name as fourth item to PoW is on the https://github.com/iljah/p2pIM/blob/main/TODO list. server1.py mentioned at end of README is my previous attempt at this (without AI help) and the one before that is probably https://github.com/iljah/a2amd in Rust.
author: iljah

title: Re: OpenAI's New ChatGPT Watermark Breaks If You Edit ...
text:
Not sure what EU regulators really expect here. There's no way to watermark plaintext that can't be circumvented in a few seconds with even very simple methods. Anybody with a Claude/Codex subscription can build their own "unwatermark text" webapp in five minutes flat. (And if Claude/Codex refuse, that's what Mimo and DeepSeek are for...)

The risk is that the quality of output, in terms of word choice and style, will decline.
